key_idea: Induct on a fractal-weighted L^p estimate where the parameters (M, γ, λ) are set up so that the narrow case's parabolic rescaling trades them off exactly, with the broad case closed by the multilinear refined Strichartz estimate.
reason: The main conceptual gain is the weighted inequality with parameters γ (α-dimensional density) and λ (local density). It is chosen so that the broad–narrow induction closes, and Intuition 23 shows why the numerology balances. However, the argument relies on several rounds of dyadic pigeonholing, locally-constant heuristics, and parameter bookkeeping. It also draws on heavy machinery (decoupling and multilinear refined Strichartz), so it is a strong, competent proof but not a book proof.
recognized: Du–Zhang, 'Sharp L^2 estimates of the Schrödinger maximal function in higher dimensions' (Annals 2019)
